first_comment: Bonus: the dogs' missing first premolars point to the same gene that makes today's Peruvian Hairless Dog bald. The breed was named part of Peru's cultural heritage in 2000. 🐕

stories.headline: A 1,200-year-old dog mummy still has its hairless skin and ears
stories.summary: At a Wari Empire site north of Lima, scientists studied bones from at least 19 dogs. One naturally mummified skull, painted red with cinnabar, kept its hairless skin and ears.
stories.why: It may be early proof of today's Peruvian Hairless Dog, a national treasure.

stories.headline: Deep-sea 'spaghetti worms' with suckers get a new genus
stories.summary: Worms collected 467 to 674 m down off Christmas Island and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands have sucker-like pads no other spaghetti worm has. DNA showed they form a whole new genus.
stories.why: One voyage's haul held 7 new species in this paper alone, and more to come.

stories.headline: A retired couple's broken furnace was replaced for free
stories.summary: Diane and Brian Johnsen's old system couldn't be fixed, and Diane was working 3 jobs to cover the mortgage. Lennox's Feel the Love program and Aviator Heating & Cooling installed a new one at no cost.
stories.why: The program has helped over 3,100 families since 2009.

stories.headline: A village knitted fake traffic cops, and drivers hit the brakes
stories.summary: After crashes near a primary school, Fillongley's Knit and Natter group made life-size knitted officers and speed cameras. The mayor says you can see brake lights come on as cars pass.
stories.why: 11 crashes in 4 years at one junction got the knitters to act.

fun_fact: The Peruvian Hairless Dog is one of only a few hairless dog breeds in the world.
